recent_posts.title: Why operational technology is the biggest hidden risk in critical infrastructure security
recent_posts.summary: Operational Technology (OT) — the systems controlling physical processes in critical national infrastructure like power, water, and transport — represents a growing and underappreciated cybersecurity risk. Originally built for isolation and physical security, these systems are now networked and remotely accessible, yet lack proper asset inventories, network documentation, and resilience planning. Geopolitically-motivated threat actors increasingly target OT to cause societal disruption or conduct long-term surveillance. Key gaps include poor asset visibility, weak IT/OT segmentation, shared identity systems, and inadequate recovery planning. Recommended steps include building and maintaining accurate OT asset inventories, reviewing identity controls, stress-testing resilience plans, and implementing OT-layer monitoring.

recent_posts.title: 86% of phishing attacks are now AI driven according to KnowBe4 report
recent_posts.summary: KnowBe4's Phishing Threat Trends Report Volume Seven reveals that 86% of phishing attacks are now AI-driven. Key findings from the last six months include a 49% increase in calendar invite phishing, a 139% surge in reverse proxy use to steal Microsoft 365 credentials, and a 41% rise in Microsoft Teams attacks. The report highlights a shift from single-vector attacks to multi-channel orchestration, with internal team impersonation appearing in 30% of Q1 2026 attacks. Cybercriminals are expanding beyond email to target collaboration tools and calendars, making social engineering more targeted and harder to detect.

recent_posts.title: Lessons from the PocketOS Incident: When AI Agents Go Beyond Their Limits
recent_posts.summary: The PocketOS incident, where an AI agent deleted a live production database and its backups in 9 seconds, is examined as a systemic security failure rather than a simple AI malfunction. Security experts highlight that the agent had over-permissioned API tokens, no real-time monitoring, and no human oversight — a cascade of failures including poor access control, insufficient API governance, and inadequate backup isolation. Experts argue AI agents must be treated as a new class of identity requiring dedicated permissions, behavioral baselines, and real-time auditability. The core lesson: autonomous systems operating at machine speed inside trust boundaries represent a new form of insider risk, and behavioral instructions alone are not enforcement.

recent_posts.title: Forescout launches global partner tour across 90 cities focused on IoT and OT security
recent_posts.summary: Forescout has announced Mission:Possible, its largest-ever global partner initiative spanning 90+ cities across May–September 2026. The campaign uses a gamified, story-driven format where partners act as 'agents' completing cybersecurity missions. Events will cover IT, OT, IoT, and IoMT security challenges, with sessions on asset visibility, Zero Trust Network Access (UZTNA), and Continuous Threat Exposure Management (CTEM). Key cities include London, Munich, Johannesburg, Mumbai, Sydney, and Kuala Lumpur, with some events hosted at iconic football stadiums. The initiative aims to drive partner pipeline growth and equip channel partners with practical tools for customer engagements.

recent_posts.title: Best AI security tools for exposure assessment in 2026
recent_posts.summary: A comparison of six AI-powered continuous threat exposure management (CTEM) platforms evaluated across four criteria: AI capability, prioritization, coverage, and automation. Tenable One leads overall with high marks across all categories, followed by Palo Alto Prisma Cloud and Microsoft Defender. Wiz and Orca Security excel in cloud-native scenarios, while CrowdStrike Falcon is positioned as a complement to rather than replacement for full CTEM solutions. The piece includes a scoring table and guidance on which platform fits different organizational needs.

recent_posts.title: Beyond the perimeter: Why identity and cyber security are one single story
recent_posts.summary: Identity and cyber security are converging as traditional network perimeters dissolve. With cloud services, distributed workforces, and automated fraud, identity is now a core component of the cyber security control surface rather than a separate discipline. The post outlines three pillars for bridging the two: identity profiling and risk scoring, contextual monitoring, and noise reduction through mature IAM. It also frames zero trust not as a product but as a design principle requiring identity assurance, authorisation, and monitoring to operate from a shared risk model. Secure-by-design thinking embeds fraud prevention into services by default rather than bolting security on afterward.

recent_posts.title: DORA and the Practical Test of Operational Resilience
recent_posts.summary: DORA (Digital Operational Resilience Act), in force since January 2025, sets strict requirements for EU financial services firms around IT risk management, resilience testing, incident handling, and third-party oversight. Despite over a year of application, 96% of EMEA financial services organizations still feel they need to improve resilience. A key gap identified is maintaining operational control during severe incidents — when primary network access is unavailable or locked down for containment. Out-of-band (independent) management infrastructure is presented as a practical solution, allowing engineers to reach critical systems, restore configurations, and recover services even when the production network is impaired. Third-party supply chain risk is also highlighted, with Verizon's 2025 DBIR noting third-party breach involvement doubled to 30%.

recent_posts.title: NCSC chief warns of ‘perfect storm’ as cyber threats intensify at CyberUK
recent_posts.summary: NCSC CEO Richard Horne warned at CyberUK 2025 in Glasgow that organisations face a 'perfect storm' of escalating cyber threats driven by AI advances and geopolitical tensions. He stressed that most successful attacks still exploit basic weaknesses like unpatched systems and legacy infrastructure, while nation-state actors are increasingly behind the most serious incidents. Industry leaders echoed concerns about the widening gap between threat sophistication and organisational readiness, particularly for SMEs. Key themes included AI compressing the time between vulnerability disclosure and exploitation, the need to embed cyber resilience as a core business priority, and emerging risks like quantum computing's 'harvest now, decrypt later' threat.

recent_posts.title: CyberSmart Partners with Renaissance to Deliver Complete Cyber Confidence for SMEs
recent_posts.summary: Irish reseller Renaissance has formed a strategic partnership with UK-based cybersecurity provider CyberSmart to bring continuous cyber protection to SMEs across Ireland. The partnership covers real-time threat detection, vulnerability management, automated patching, compliance assurance (Cyber Essentials Plus, ISO 27001, NIS2), and cybersecurity awareness training. CyberSmart's platform supports remote work and BYOD environments and will be offered through Renaissance to enterprises, MSPs, and MSSPs. CyberSmart's CEO noted that only 1 in 4 businesses report full NIS2 compliance despite the 2024 deadline, citing budget constraints and confusion as key barriers.

recent_posts.title: Bridewell Among First to Achieve Level 2 Defence Cyber Certification
recent_posts.summary: Bridewell has become one of the first organisations to achieve Level 2 Defence Cyber Certification (DCC), a UK Ministry of Defence scheme delivered by IASME to standardise cyber security across the defence supply chain. Level 2 requires meeting 139 controls and demonstrating mature cyber risk management, targeting contracts with moderate to high risk profiles. Only two organisations hold this accreditation currently. Bridewell also participated in the scheme's rollout as an early certification body and plans to help other organisations navigate the certification process from gap analysis to ongoing compliance.

top_posts.title: Can AI replace the CEO? Zuckerberg's Meta agent sparks debate
top_posts.summary: Mark Zuckerberg is developing a personal AI agent to streamline executive decision-making at Meta, reigniting debate about whether AI could replace C-suite leadership. Meta has already deployed internal AI tools like 'Second Brain' and 'My Claw', and reports a 30% rise in engineer output since 2025. Security and tech leaders push back on the replacement narrative, warning of deskilling risks, data leakage, deepfake manipulation, and accountability gaps if AI takes over leadership roles. The consensus from experts is that AI will reshape leadership rather than replace it, but executives who fail to adapt risk being outcompeted by those who embrace it.

top_posts.title: CREST introduces a staged pathway for advancement to globally-recognised CREST cybersecurity accreditation
top_posts.summary: CREST has launched Pathway and Pathway+ programs to help cybersecurity organizations work toward full accreditation through a staged approach. The Pathway stage provides access to CREST resources and communities, while Pathway+ adds self-assessment tools and potential mentoring opportunities. Organizations can progress from Pathway to full accreditation within four years, or from Pathway+ within two years. These programs aim to build industry capacity while maintaining rigorous standards for cybersecurity service providers in areas like penetration testing, threat intelligence, and incident response.

top_posts.title: How to Secure Your Promo Codes Against Cyber Exploits
top_posts.summary: Promotional codes face significant security risks from cybercriminals who steal, hijack, or create fraudulent coupons to exploit businesses and customers. Key protection strategies include implementing real-time monitoring systems, setting clear usage restrictions with expiration dates and geographic limitations, using automated anti-fraud tools with alerts, and securing distribution platforms through verified affiliate networks. These measures help prevent revenue loss, protect customer data, and maintain brand reputation.

top_posts.title: It’s Never Too Late: Transitioning to a Career in Cybersecurity
top_posts.summary: Michael Keddie shares his journey from being a History teacher to becoming a cybersecurity consultant. He highlights the significance of taking risks, learning new skills, and being resilient in the pursuit of a new career. Lockdown provided him the time to reflect and pursue a part-time MSc in Computer Science with Cybersecurity, leading to his position as a training academy team leader at Pentest People. He encourages those considering a mid-life career change to embrace the life-affirming and revitalizing experience.

top_posts.title: Key software practices driving business success
top_posts.summary: The post outlines ten crucial software development practices that are key to modern business success. These practices include Agile methodologies, CI/CD, TDD, microservices architecture, and cloud-native development, among others. Each practice contributes to faster delivery, enhanced user satisfaction, better scalability, and robust security measures, positioning businesses to thrive in a competitive digital environment.
